ai.literal: Many people to be disgusted, useless things he who speaks, by everyone to be despised will experience.
ai.translation: He who speaks useless words, causing many to be disgusted, will be despised by everyone.
ai.modern: பலர் வெறுக்கும்படியாகப் பயனில்லாத சொற்களைப் பேசுபவன், எல்லாராலும் இகழப்படுவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the social consequences of speaking without substance. When a person constantly utters useless words, it first causes annoyance and disgust (முனிய) among those who are listening. Eventually, this habit ruins their reputation entirely, leading to universal contempt and mockery (எள்ளப்படும்) from everyone in society. The progression from the irritation of a few to the contempt of all highlights how idle talk destroys one's standing.

ai.literal: Speaking useless things before many people is worse than doing things devoid of goodness towards friends.
ai.translation: To speak useless words in the presence of many is worse than doing deeds devoid of kindness to one's friends.
ai.modern: பலர் முன்னிலையில் பயனில்லாத சொற்களைப் பேசுவது, நண்பர்களுக்கு நன்மை இல்லாத தீய செயல்களைச் செய்வதை விடக் கொடியதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the severe consequences of speaking useless words in public. The poet compares two wrongdoings: performing unkind or harmful deeds toward one's friends, and speaking empty, profitless words in front of a large gathering. While harming friends is a grave moral failing, the poet declares that uttering useless words in public is even worse. This is because public babbling instantly exposes one's lack of wisdom, ruins one's reputation, and wastes the collective time of many people.

ai.literal: "He lacks goodness" that fact will reveal, the useless, elaborately spoken words.
ai.translation: The useless words spoken at great length by a person will themselves proclaim that he is devoid of all goodness.
ai.modern: பயனற்ற சொற்களை விரிவாகப் பேசும் பேச்சு, ஒருவன் நற்பண்பு இல்லாதவன் என்பதை வெளிப்படுத்தும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how speaking useless words exposes a person's character. When someone speaks at great length about trivial and useless matters, their own speech acts as a giveaway. It reveals to everyone that the speaker lacks goodness and virtue. Thus, empty talk not only wastes time but also ruins one's reputation by exposing a lack of inner worth.

ai.literal: Righteousness not aligning with, from goodness will separate, utility not yielding, courtesy lacking words, many people in the presence of.
ai.translation: Words that lack courtesy and yield no benefit, when spoken in the presence of many, will alienate the speaker from righteousness and strip them of all goodness.
ai.modern: பலர் முன்னிலையில் பேசப்படும் பயனில்லாத, நற்பண்பு இல்லாத சொற்கள், ஒருவனை அறநெறியிலிருந்து விலக்கி, அவனுக்குக் கிடைக்கும் நன்மைகளிலிருந்தும் நீக்கிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the severe consequences of speaking useless and discourteous words in public. The poet describes such speech as 'பயன் சாராப் பண்பில் சொல்'—words that lack utility and basic human decency. When spoken in the presence of many ('பல்லார் அகத்து'), these words do not align with righteousness ('நயன் சாரா') and actively drag the speaker away from all goodness ('நன்மையின் நீக்கும்'). Thus, empty and rude speech in public ruins a person's moral standing and deprives them of the benefits of a virtuous life.

ai.literal: Greatness along with glory will depart, if those who possess good nature speak useless things.
ai.translation: If people of noble character speak useless words, their greatness, along with their glory, will depart from them.
ai.modern: நற்குணங்களை உடையவர்கள் பயனில்லாத சொற்களைப் பேசினால், அவர்களுடைய பெருமையும் சிறப்பும் அவர்களை விட்டு நீங்கிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns that even people who naturally possess a good and noble character (நீர்மையுடையார்) will lose their standing if they indulge in useless talk. The word 'சீர்மை' refers to their inherent greatness or dignity, while 'சிறப்பு' refers to the external glory or distinction they have earned. Both of these qualities will vanish (நீங்கும்) the moment they speak words that lack substance or benefit (பயனில). Thus, the poet emphasizes that maintaining one's reputation requires constant vigilance over one's speech.

words.gloss: him who speaks useless words repeatedly

ai.literal: Calling him who speaks words without usefulness a man is calling him the chaff of humanity.
ai.translation: To call a person who repeatedly utters useless words a human being is like calling empty chaff a grain.
ai.modern: பயனற்ற சொற்களைப் பேசித் திரிகிறவனை மனிதன் என்று சொல்லக் கூடாது; அவனை மனிதர்களுள் பதர் (பயனற்ற உமி) என்றுதான் சொல்ல வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a powerful agricultural metaphor to describe someone who speaks useless words. Just as chaff (பதடி) looks like grain from the outside but contains no substance inside, a person who speaks without purpose or utility may look like a human being (மகன்) but lacks any real human worth. The word 'பாராட்டுவான்' here refers to one who repeatedly utters or dwells on useless talk. The author emphasizes that such a person should not be counted among true human beings, but rather dismissed as empty chaff.

ai.literal: Even if they speak things devoid of pleasantness, let the noble people speak them; but not speaking things devoid of usefulness is good.
ai.translation: Even if noble people speak words devoid of pleasantness, it is still better for them to completely refrain from speaking words devoid of usefulness.
ai.modern: சான்றோர்கள் அறநெறி அல்லது இனிமை இல்லாத சொற்களைச் சொன்னாலும் சொல்லலாம்; ஆனால், பயனில்லாத சொற்களைச் சொல்லாமல் இருப்பது அவர்களுக்கு மிகவும் நல்லது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute necessity of avoiding useless chatter by comparing it with unpleasant speech. The author suggests that even if wise and noble people (சான்றோர்) happen to utter words lacking in pleasantness or virtue (நயனில), it may be tolerated. However, it is of paramount importance and goodness (நன்று) that they never speak words that are completely devoid of utility or purpose (பயனில). This comparison emphasizes that while harsh or unvirtuous words might occasionally occur under specific circumstances, useless words serve no purpose at all and must be strictly avoided.

ai.literal: Those of wisdom who examine rare benefits will not speak words that do not have great benefit.
ai.translation: Those who possess the wisdom to seek rare and precious benefits will never utter words that are devoid of great utility.
ai.modern: அரிய நன்மைகளை ஆராய்ந்து அறியும் அறிவுடையவர்கள், பெரிய பயன் தராத வீணான சொற்களைப் பேச மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the connection between wisdom and purposeful speech. Wise individuals are described as those who analyze and seek rare, valuable benefits (arumpayan āyum aṟiviṉār). Because they value substance and truth, they naturally refrain from speaking words that lack any significant utility or great benefit (perumpayan illātha sol). The contrast between seeking 'rare benefits' and avoiding 'useless words' teaches us that true intellect is reflected in the fruitfulness of one's speech.

words.gloss: those who have vision or knowledge

ai.literal: Meaning-devoid [words], even by forgetfulness, will not speak, delusion-devoid, blemish-free vision-having-people.
ai.translation: Those who possess flawless vision, free from delusion, will not speak words devoid of meaning, even by a slip of the mind.
ai.modern: மயக்கம் நீங்கிய, குற்றமற்ற அறிவை உடையவர்கள், மறந்தும் கூடப் பயனில்லாத சொற்களைச் சொல்ல மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains that wise people with clear, flawless understanding (மாசறு காட்சியவர்) who are free from delusion (மருள்தீர்ந்த) will never utter useless or meaningless words (பொருள்தீர்ந்த). The word 'பொச்சாந்தும்' (even by forgetfulness) is crucial here; it emphasizes that their self-control and clarity of mind are so deep-rooted that they will not let a useless word slip out even accidentally or in a moment of inattention. Their speech is a direct reflection of their pure, unblemished wisdom.

ai.literal: Speak, in speech, words possessing usefulness; do not speak, in speech, words lacking usefulness.
ai.translation: If you speak, speak only words that have usefulness; do not speak words that are devoid of any benefit.
ai.modern: பேசினால் பயனுள்ள வார்த்தைகளைப் பேசுங்கள்; பயனில்லாத வார்த்தைகளைப் பேசாதீர்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet concludes the chapter on avoiding useless talk with a direct and memorable command. The author advises that if one must speak, they should choose only those words that carry meaning, benefit, or utility. Conversely, one must completely avoid uttering words that are empty and yield no positive outcome. By repeating the structure of speaking and not speaking, the verse emphasizes that speech is a tool to be used purposefully, and silence is far superior to useless chatter.
